title: Gaia DR3 eclipse times from 2014-2017 confirm the ASAS-3-to-TESS period changes of southern detached binaries; their size agrees with third stars on decade orbits, not with a constant period drift
abstract: SCI 02d77ae9 found that 77 of 304 detached southern ACVS binaries (P = 5-22 d) have common-mode eclipse-time changes between ASAS-3 (2000-2009) and TESS (2018-2026), and interpreted them as light travel time (LTTE) from third stars on decade orbits. We tested this with a third, independent epoch: Gaia DR3 G-band epoch photometry (2014.6-2017.4). For 174 binaries with Gaia data we fitted empirical eclipse templates from each binary's own TESS QLP light curve to the sparse Gaia points and measured one time offset per eclipse kind. The error scale (1.28) comes from primary-secondary agreement. 48 common-mode binaries and 90 link-test passes (controls) give good offsets. Gaia departs from the TESS ephemeris by more than 3 sigma in 24 of 48 common-mode binaries and in 8 of 90 controls (Fisher p = 1.2e-7). In 21 of the 24 the sign agrees with a smooth ASAS-3-to-TESS path (p = 1.4e-4); Gaia offsets correlate with that prediction (Spearman 0.68, p = 8e-8). Gaia blindly tests published LTTE orbits: ASAS 063202-6750.7 agrees with its 16.9-yr orbit (predicted -23.8 +- 1.5, measured -22.3 +- 2.4 min) and rejects 8-9-yr alternatives by 14 sigma; ASAS 115007-6425.1 rejects its 7.3-yr best orbit (6.7 sigma) and favours the 20-yr solution; two other orbits agree within 1.1 sigma. Simulations with the real sampling show that detected tertiaries with P2 = 15-50 yr (or the field log-normal) reproduce the departure rate (0.50) and the slopes on three predictions, while near-constant period drifts give a rate of 0.10 and 50-200-yr orbits 0.27 (both p < 0.005). Limits: one Gaia epoch per binary; few in-eclipse points; 8.9 percent of controls also depart; the simulation assumes LTTE from one tertiary and does not measure the tertiary fraction; no spectroscopy.

Gaia confirms the 16.9-yr orbit of ASAS 063202-6750.7 and the 20-yr solution of ASAS 115007-6425.1.

(a) Gaia offsets against the Hermite ASAS-3-to-TESS prediction for 48 common-mode binaries and 90 controls. (b) Fraction of binaries above a given |Gaia offset|/sigma from the TESS ephemeris.
